strategies.name: Hard start, 2-stop
strategies.label: H→M→M (L28, L48)
rules: Stay on the planned stop laps; if stuck, keep trying to pass and accept the tyre cost.
Safety car / VSC with tyres ≥ 8 laps old and a stop still to make → box (stop costs ~50 % under SC, ~70 % under VSC).
Red flag → free tyre change; pick the compound by remaining distance (≥40 laps hard, 22-39 medium, otherwise soft).

qa.a: Start ≈ 92 kg, finish ≈ 1.5 kg (≈ 1.37 kg/lap). Car + driver minimum is 768 kg without fuel (FIA 2026), so the car races at ≈ 860 kg on the grid and ≈ 770 kg at the flag. 2026 has no per-race fuel mass cap; the figure is derived from the 3000 MJ/h energy-flow limit (71 kg/h at 42 MJ/kg → 84-95 kg for 80-90 % duty). Treat it as ±8 kg.

Anchored to the 2026 pole lap 1:14.679 (soft, qualifying trim). Race pace, fresh tyre, clean air: Soft 1:21.779 on lap 2 → 1:20.351 mid-race → 1:19.135 light; Medium +0.55 s; Hard +1.10 s on the same fuel. Real race fastest laps were 1:20.1-1:20.6, which this reproduces.

Early-stint slope (s/lap): Soft 0.102, Medium 0.055, Hard 0.036 at 25 °C air. The cliff starts around lap 10 (Soft), 19 (Medium) and 29 (Hard) of a stint; total pace lost vs a fresh tyre after 10 / 20 / 30 laps: Soft 1.1 / 7.1 / 21.8 s, Medium 0.6 / 1.2 / 4.2 s, Hard 0.4 / 0.7 / 1.1 s. Pirelli describes Barcelona degradation as predominantly thermal with the front axle limiting, so wear accelerates above 100 °C surface temperature. These rates are priors: fetch_fastf1.py can replace them with fuel-corrected fits.

qa.q: Highest speed on each corner and straight
qa.a: Model apex speeds run from 115 km/h (T10) to 276 km/h (T9); top speed ≈ 328 km/h on T14-T1, with the start/finish straight (1145 m) reaching ≈ 328 km/h. Full table is on the Track tab. Source: schematic reconstruction (corner table + calibrated point-mass model).

qa.q: Pit-lane speed limit and pit delta
qa.a: Pit-lane limit 80 km/h (verify against the FIA event notes). Green-flag time loss ≈ 21.5 s (σ 0.5 s, 4 % chance of a 2-6 s slow stop); under SC ≈ 10.8 s, under VSC ≈ 15.0 s.

Starting P4 with the field on typical strategies: best 1-stop H→M (L38): podium 39 %, E[finish] P7.6; best 2-stop H→M→M (L28, L48): podium 55 %, E[finish] P4.6; best 3-stop S→M→S→M (L11, L31, L43): podium 27 %, E[finish] P6.8. Green-flag, no-traffic race times differ by single-digit seconds between stop counts, so track position and neutralisations decide it.

qa.q: Stuck behind a car: overtake or pit?
qa.a: Within 1.2 s a pass is attempted each lap with probability = logistic((pace edge − 0.70 s)/0.30); the follower is held at ≥ 0.65 s otherwise, runs 5 °C hotter and wears 25 % faster. The strategy search compares 'keep trying' against 'undercut after 3 or 5 stuck laps'; break-even tables are on the Risk tab.

qa.q: Chances of VSC, SC and red flag
qa.a: Per-race: SC ≈ 33 %, VSC ≈ 24 %, red flag ≈ 5 %, any neutralisation ≈ 52 %. A neutralisation lands inside the first stop window (laps 12-26) in ≈ 17 % of races.

Fuel burn (lighter car each lap), thermal tyre window 85-110 °C and thermal wear acceleration, dirty-air heating, out-lap warm-up, standing-start loss, slow stops, SC bunching, reduced SC/VSC pit cost, red-flag free tyres, field strategy mix with SC reactions, common random numbers across strategies. Not modelled: lapped traffic, penalties, weather change, ERS state-of-charge per car, tyre-set availability, damage, driver-specific skill.
